set.name: Signal
set.mechanism: An E assembled from four separate bars, with the middle bar lit in cyan: precise modules plus one live signal. The same bar-and-gap rule sets the grid, the type and the glow.
set.expression_move: The cyan signal bar is the only bright thing, glowing on midnight.
set.differs_by: The references (Linear, Stripe) own indigo and violet; Vercel owns black and white. Signal holds midnight navy with cyan, a hue only about 2-12% of software marks use, and keeps violet to a faint glow.

logo.concept: A segmented E: three arms and a stem that never touch, the middle arm lit. Software is built from parts that fit precisely; ElIT supplies the signal that makes them run.

misuse.label: Do not close the gaps between the bars
Do not light a different bar

defaults_used.why: The user asked for midnight navy. It is a dark ground here, not a finance-style primary, and cyan does the identifying.
The user asked for a subtle violet. It is kept as a glow and chart colour only, never a primary or text colour, so it stays apart from Linear's and Stripe's indigo.

rationale.claim: Moderustic has no tabular figures, so Geologica carries running text and numbers, and JetBrains Mono carries code, which is native territory for a software company.
Every letter of ElIT (E, l, I, T) is made of straight bars, so a bar module is native to the name rather than imposed on it.
Moderustic's lowercase l has a tail, so ElIT can't be misread as EIIT. Most geometric sans faces draw l and I identically.
Cyan is used in about 2-12% of marks in the logo library's developer, cloud and productivity categories; blue in 19-28%.

palette.name: Signal
palette.direction: Midnight navy grounds (#0B1531), one ion-cyan signal, a faint aurora violet glow.

set.name: Frame
set.mechanism: Two chamfered corner brackets hold one ember core: ElIT is the frame that every product is built inside. The chamfer is cut from Tektur's angled corners, and the frame becomes the container for every future product.
set.expression_move: The ember core square is the only colour; everything else is graphite on concrete.
set.differs_by: The references are dark or blue-violet with soft gradients. Frame is light concrete with graphite and a single hot ember point, angular and engineered rather than glowing.

logo.concept: Two chamfered brackets frame a core: the frame is the company, the core is whatever it builds. Each future product sits in the same frame with its own core colour.

rationale.claim: Tektur's capital I has slab serifs, so ElIT stays legible: the l is a plain stem, the I is serifed.
An umbrella brand needs a container: product marks reuse the brackets with their own core colour, so every product is visibly ElIT-built without sharing a name.
Concrete grey plus graphite keeps the ground neutral; ember is the only hue (a single-accent structure).

set.name: Edition
set.mechanism: A sharp high-contrast serif wordmark in cobalt ink, with one cobalt-weight overline floating above IT: software presented with an editorial, premium hand, and the IT inside the name underlined from above.
set.expression_move: The overline above IT in the serif wordmark; everything else stays porcelain, ink and cobalt.
set.differs_by: Every reference uses a sans-serif and a symbol. Edition is wordmark-only and serif, a rare position (wordmarks are 3-15% of the library's software marks), reading as studio and partner rather than another startup.

logo.concept: ElIT set in a cut serif with a solid overline above IT: the name read as El + IT, a rule that later carries product names.

extra: #5EF0C0:Signal Mint:status and data highlights on dark surfaces only

defaults_used.why: Flagged on Ink #0E1124, a near-black text colour with a blue tint so it sits with cobalt. It is not used as a navy brand colour; cobalt is the identifying colour.

rationale.claim: Serifs distinguish the I from the l, so ElIT reads correctly in a serif without any trick.
Wordmark-only marks are 3-15% of the library's developer, cloud and productivity logos, so this is an open position on the shelf.
A single deep cobalt as ink (rather than as a large surface) keeps the palette quiet so the type can speak.

palette.name: Edition
palette.direction: Cobalt ink on porcelain, with a small signal mint for live data.
